Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Replay loot: the first local-world experiment

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Run from the repository root:

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_loot/run.sh

This is a standalone Odin executable; Godot, sockets, and generated scripts are not involved. It exercises the new Replay library. Existing games remain available in their original directories.

Two players stand beside a chest with five items. The initial input says player one takes it. After eight ticks, a revised input says player two took it instead. Replay restores the whole world and rebuilds those ticks. Both inventories, the chest's destruction, projectile lifetime/allocation, RNG, and occurrence history are managed by that same operation.

The executable verifies the corrected result against an independent run that received the correct input from the start. It also copies the frame at tick four and continues in a fresh timeline under a new event epoch. This is an in-process checkpoint test, not a host migration demo.

Expected final receipts:

Text
REPLAY_LOOT predicted=5,0 corrected=0,5 replayed=8 checkpoint_tick=4
REPLAY_LOOT_OK
  • game/game.odin: the complete gameplay model, shared by the demo and property/behavior tests.
  • main.odin: local timeline, input correction, reference run, resume.
  • ../../tests/replay/replay_test.odin: failure atomicity, history limits, event replacement, handle lifetime, type constraints, and reproducibility tests.

The Godot loot view now uses this same model and tests effect cancellation while correcting the winner. The complete port and comparison sequence is in the roadmap.
